text: Every Monday, from eight to ten in the evening.
Split the sentence into tokens, keeping each word's position.
Each word becomes numerical features: its spelling, its shape, and its neighbors.
One tiny neural network turns those features into fifteen scores per token.
These are raw model scores. For Monday, the highest score is weekday.
The model labels the words. Code handles the meaning.
Code builds the schedule: every Monday, eight to ten, in New York.
Eight in the evening stays fixed, even when daylight saving changes the U T C time.
Export calendar rules from the same schedule.
G P U time. Plain English. Precise schedules.
